questions.question: Which benefit to a LAN does a switch provide?
choices: Allows for a fast uplink port
questions.explanation: Switches break up collision domains by allowing full-duplex. Switches are set to auto-negotiate duplex and speed by default, and they do not force full-duplex.

questions.question: Where are MAC address tables stored?
questions.explanation: MAC address tables, also called CAM tables, are always built and stored temporarily in RAM. When the switch is turned off or the clear command is issued, the table no longer exists.

questions.question: Which advantage(s) are gained using switches?
questions.explanation: Switches allow for low latency because frames are forwarded. They utilize ASIC hardware-based switching and have low cost.

questions.question: How do switches forward frames only to the destination computer?
choices: Forward filter decisions based on the MAC address table
Flooding ports for the destination MAC address
Forward filter decisions based on the routing table
questions.explanation: Switches make forward/filter decisions based upon the MAC address to port association in the MAC address table.

questions.question: Which mechanism does a switch employ to stop switching loops?
questions.explanation: The mechanism that switches use for loop avoidance is STP, or Spanning Tree Protocol.

questions.question: How are MAC addresses learned and associated with the port?
questions.explanation: Switches learn MAC addresses by inspecting the frame’s source MAC address on the incoming port. They then associate the source MAC address with the port it came in on.

questions.question: Which command will allow you to see the MAC address table?
questions.explanation: The command to see the MAC address table is show mac address- table . However, on some 4000 and 6500 series switches, show cam dynamic will perform the same function.

questions.question: Which statement is true of an ARP request entering into a switch?
choices: The switch will respond directly back with an ARP reply.
The switch will only forward the ARP request to the port for the destination computer.
The source MAC address of the frame will be all F s.
The destination MAC address of the frame will be all F s.
questions.explanation: The destination MAC address for broadcasts are always all F s, such as ffff.ffff.ffff.

questions.question: Which command will display all connected ports on a switch and include descriptions?
questions.explanation: The show interfaces status command will display the port number, connected status, VLAN, duplex, speed, and type of interface.
questions.topic: 2.3 Troubleshoot interface and cable issues (collisions, errors, duplex, speed)

questions.question: Which is a consequence of not using loop avoidance with layer 2 switching?
questions.explanation: When loop avoidance such as STP is not employed and loops exist, you will get duplicate unicast frames and broadcast storms. This will inevitably thrash the MAC address table and degrade bandwidth to nothing.

questions.question: What is the default MAC address aging time for dynamic entries on most switches?
questions.explanation: The default MAC address aging time for dynamic entries is 300 seconds, or 5 minutes.

questions.question: Which is a correct statement when hubs are replaced with switches?
questions.explanation: The replacement of hubs with switches increases collision domains and effectively increases bandwidth.

questions.question: Which command will show the number of entries in a MAC address table?
questions.explanation: The command to show the current MAC address entry count in the MAC address table is show mac address-table count . This command will also show the maximum number of entries the table can hold.

questions.question: When a switch receives a frame, what does it use to make a forwarding decision?
choices: Source IP address in the frame
Source MAC address in the frame
Destination IP address in the frame
Destination MAC address in the frame
questions.explanation: Forward filter decisions are made upon the destination MAC address in the frame.

questions.question: Which switching method checks the CRC as the frame is received by the switch?
questions.explanation: Store-and-forward mode is the default mode for mode edge switching equipment. Store-and-forward receives the frame, calculates the CRC, and then makes a forwarding decision.

questions.question: Which statement is true about collision domains?
choices: All computers in the collision domain are set to 10 Mb/s full-duplex.
All computers in the collision domain have the potential to receive layer 2 broadcast messages.
All computers in the collision domain have the potential to have a frame collision.
All computers in the collision domain have the potential to receive layer 3 broadcast messages.
questions.explanation: A collision domain is defined as a group of computers that can potentially have a frame collision. Adding switches that can negotiate full- duplex and forward/filter fixes these issues.

questions.question: Which switch mode operation reads only the first 64 bytes before making a switching decision?
questions.explanation: Fragment-free mode reads the first 64 bytes and deems the frame intact and forwardable. This is because most collisions that would create frame fragments happen within the first 64 bytes of a frame. This method of switching is often found on SOHO switching equipment.

questions.question: Which protocol on the host machine allows for a mapping of IP to MAC address?
questions.explanation: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is used to map remote IPs on the current LAN to MAC addresses. It does this by broadcasting at layer 2 to all nodes for a response for the MAC address. Thus, it is a mapping of IP address to MAC address.

questions.question: Which protocol on the host machine allows for a mapping of MAC to IP address?
questions.explanation: Reverse Address Resolution Protocol (RARP) is used to map MAC addresses on the current LAN to IPs. BOOTP also uses this method to allocate an IP address via the MAC address. Thus, it is a mapping of MAC address to IP address.

questions.question: Which command would you use to reset the MAC address table for learned MAC addresses in a switch?
questions.explanation: The command used to reset the MAC address table is clear mac- address-table dynamic .

questions.question: You need to see all of the MAC addresses associated with a single interface. Which command would you use?
questions.explanation: The command to see all of the MAC addresses on a single interface is show mac address-table interfaces fast 0/1 . This command can be entered in either privileged exec mode or user exec mode.

questions.question: Which switch mode operation reads only the first 6 bytes before making a switching decision?
questions.explanation: Cut-through mode copies the first 6 bytes after the preamble into memory and makes a switching decision on the destination MAC address. Many data center switches use this method of switching to provide low latency while assuming no collisions will exist.

questions.question: Which option describes latency in switching?
choices: The delay between switching the frame to the destination interface
The delay in forward lookups to forward frames
The delay in forward lookups to forward packets
The delay between routing packets to the destination interface
questions.explanation: Latency in switching is the total time it takes to forward an incoming frame to its destination interface. Latency of frame forwarding adversely affects total bandwidth.

questions.question: Which is attributed to lowering switch latency?
choices: The use of higher bandwidth connections
questions.explanation: Hardware-based bridging uses specialized application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) to provide low latency in switching frames.

questions.question: What is the difference between a broadcast frame and a flooded frame?
choices: A broadcast frame and a flooded frame are the same.
Flooding of frames only occurs if there are switching loops.
A broadcast frame contains a destination MAC address beginning with ff:ff:ff.
A flooded frame is a frame that is unknown in the MAC address table.
questions.explanation: Flooding occurs only when the destination MAC address is not in the current MAC address table.

questions.question: What is the most accurate definition of wire speed with switching?
choices: The switch can process requests at the incoming and outgoing speed of the connection.
The switch can auto-negotiate between several different wire speeds.
The switch can process requests at the incoming speed of the connection.
Switching between two ports can happen at wire speed.
questions.explanation: Wire speed is the switch’s ability to process packets both incoming and outgoing on the same port at wire speed. However, this is not the switch’s ability to switch at that speed; the speed of the switch is limited by its backplane bandwidth.

questions.question: Which is a function of a layer 2 switch?
choices: Learning the MAC address by examining the destination MAC addresses
Forwarding the date based upon logical addressing
Repeating the electrical signal to all ports
Determining the forwarding interfaces based upon the destination MAC address and tables
questions.explanation: Switches learn MAC addresses based upon incoming ports and examination of the source MAC address. It will build a MAC address table for future lookups. It then determines forwarding interfaces based upon the destination MAC address contained in the frame.

questions.question: What is a reason a network administrator would segment a network with a switch?
questions.explanation: A switch creates micro-segmentation, which in turns isolates traffic between two talking computers from other computers that are not part of the communications. This in turn increases bandwidth for the computers that are not part of the communications between the two talking computers.

questions.question: If a switch uses the store and forward method of switching and receives a frame in which its CRC is invalid, what will happen?
choices: The switch will re-create the frame with a new CRC and correct the missing information.
The switch will drop the frame and wait for retransmission of a new frame.
The switch will send back a frame for retransmission of the frame.
The switch will store the frame until a new frame with a matching CRC is received.
questions.explanation: The store and forward method of switching allows the switch to receive the entire frame and calculate the CRC against the data contained in the frame. If the CRC does not match, the frame is dropped, and the sending node must retransmit after an expiry timer or upper-protocol timer times out.

questions.question: What information is added to the MAC address table when a frame is received on an interface?
choices: Destination MAC address of the frame and outgoing port number
Destination MAC address of the frame and incoming port number
Source MAC address of the frame and incoming port number
Source MAC address of the frame and outgoing port number
questions.explanation: When a frame is received on an incoming port, both the incoming port and the source MAC address are added to the MAC address table and set with an aging timer.

questions.question: What is the maximum wire speed of a single port on a 48-port Gigabit Ethernet switch?
questions.explanation: Wire speed of a single port on a 48-port gigabit switch would be 1 Gb/s, or 1,000 Mb/s.

questions.question: You need to change the default mac address aging time on a switch to 400 seconds. Which command would you use?
questions.explanation: MAC address aging time can be configured via the command mac- address-table aging-time 400 . You can additionally specify a VLAN ID.

questions.question: Which statement describes the micro-segmentation that a switch provides?
choices: Each port on the switch creates an isolation for layer 2 broadcasts.
Each port on the switch creates its own collision domain.
Each port on the switch segments broadcasts.
All of the ports on the switch create a single collision domain.
questions.explanation: Each port on a switch creates its own collision domain. An increase in collision domains raises bandwidth since each port creates its own segment (micro-segmentation) and isolates possible collisions on other ports.

questions.question: Under which circumstance will a switch drop a frame?
choices: If the destination MAC address of the frame is unknown in the MAC address table
If the source MAC address of the frame is unknown in the MAC address table
If the destination MAC address exists in another switch’s MAC address table
If the frame is deemed to be corrupt via the CRC
questions.explanation: The only time a frame is dropped is when the cyclic redundancy check (CRC) calculated against the frame’s payload deems the frame corrupt. If the destination MAC address is not known, it will be flooded to all active ports on the switch, but it will not be dropped.

questions.question: In a layer 2 frame, where is the destination MAC address?
choices: The destination MAC address is found in the preamble.
The destination MAC address is in the second 6 bytes after the preamble.
The destination MAC address is in the first 6 bytes after the preamble.
The destination MAC address is the payload data.
questions.explanation: The 6-byte destination MAC address is after the preamble/SFD so that it can be read by the switch for forwarding.

questions.question: What is the significance of the preamble?
choices: The preamble allows the switch to sync timing for the receipt of information to follow.
The preamble allows the switch to read the sequence and acknowledge receipt of the frame.
The preamble allows the switch to allocate a buffer.
The preamble allows the switch to sense collisions before data is transmitted.
questions.explanation: The preamble allows for the source computer to sync its timing of the physical media independent interface with the destination computer. It achieves this via an alternating 1 and 0 pattern at a specific frequency, depending on data transfer speed. The Start Frame Delimiter (SFD) has an extra bit to let the destination computer know anything that follows is data.

questions.question: How many bits is the OUI assigned by the IEEE?
questions.explanation: The organizationally unique identifier, or OUI, is 24 bits, or the first 3 bytes of the MAC address.

questions.question: What function does the Frame Check Sequence (FCS) perform?
choices: The FCS will error-correct data in a frame.
The FCS is used for acknowledgment of receipt of the frame.
The FCS will detect errors in a frame’s data.
questions.explanation: The Frame Check Sequence is a 4-byte cyclical redundancy check (CRC) calculation. Its only function is to detect erroneous frames; it will not correct data and contains no parity to do so.

questions.question: If the Individual/Group (I/G) bit is set to 1 in the OUI portion of the MAC address, which statement is true?
choices: The MAC address is a broadcast or multicast.
The MAC address is locally governed.
The MAC address should always be broadcast.
The MAC address is unique and governed by the IEEE.
questions.explanation: When the I/G bit is set, it means that the MAC address is intended to be a broadcast or multicast for a group of recipients.

questions.question: If the Group/Local (G/L) bit is set to 1 in the OUI portion of the MAC address, which statement is true?
choices: The MAC address is a broadcast or multicast.
The MAC address is a unique computer and governed by the IEEE.
The MAC address should always be broadcast.
The MAC address is locally governed.
questions.explanation: When the G/L bit (sometimes referred to as the U/L bit) is set, it means that the MAC address is locally governed. This means that the user has manually set the MAC address.

questions.question: Which is a reason that the Ethernet protocol uses physical addresses?
choices: It creates a differentiation between layer 2 and layer 3 communications.
It uniquely identifies devices at layer 2.
It defines a logical address scheme for devices.
It allows the node to decide if the device is remote or local.
questions.explanation: MAC addresses are physical addresses that are burned into every NIC card and network device. They are unique at the Data Link layer for direct communication purposes.

questions.question: What is the nominal MTU for LAN communications?
questions.explanation: The nominal MTU size is 1,500 bytes of data. It may also be advertised as 1,518 bytes, which is calculated from 1,500-bytes (payload) + 6 bytes (source MAC address) + 6 bytes (destination MAC address) + 2 bytes (type field) + 4 bytes (FCS) = 1,518 bytes. If 802.1Q VLAN tagging is being used, it can be advertised as 1,522 bytes to allow for 4 bytes for tagging. If ISL VLAN tagging is being used, ISL requires 30 bytes + 1,518 bytes = 1,548 bytes.

questions.question: What is the 2-byte type field used for in an Ethernet frame?
choices: It describes the length of data contained within the frame.
It is a calculation with the FCS to provide error detection.
It identifies the upper-layer protocol for the data contained within the frame.
It defines the data type contained within the frame.
questions.explanation: The Ethernet type field is 2 bytes and it identifies at layer 2 which upper-layer protocol to send the data to. When IPv4 is used, the type field is 08-00. When IPv6 is used, the type field is 86-dd.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the State Frame Delimiter byte in a frame?
choices: It provides a means for the receiving node to know when data begins.
It delimits the destination and source MAC address.
It divides the data and the physical timing portion of the frame.
It provides physical timing for the frame following.
questions.explanation: The preamble is 7 bytes of alternating 1s and 0s at a frequency that matches the bandwidth of the link. It is important to note that the 1s and 0s pattern starts with a 1 and ends with a 0 for 7 bytes (10101010). The SFD has an extra lower bit signaling the end of timing and the start of data (10101011).

questions.question: You have just resolved a problem and now need to monitor the problem on the interface. How would you reset the error counts for a single interface?
questions.explanation: In order to clear the counters for a single interface, you would use the command clear counters interface fast 0/1 . After it’s entered, you will need to confirm clearing of the counters. Then you can monitor the solution provided on the interface.
questions.topic: 2.3 Troubleshoot interface and cable issues (collisions, errors, duplex, speed)

questions.question: You have statically set an interface to 100 Mb/s full-duplex. However, the device you are plugging in will not work. Which command would you use to set speed and duplex back to auto-negotiate?
questions.explanation: The commands to set the port back to auto-negotiation are speed auto and duplex auto . You can also negate the command with no speed and no duplex commands. Both methods will set auto-negotiation back on the port.
questions.topic: 2.3 Troubleshoot interface and cable issues (collisions, errors, duplex, speed)

questions.question: You have auto-negotiation turned off on the node, but it is turned on at the switch’s interface connecting the node. The interface is a 10/100/1000 Mb/s interface and the node is 100 Mb/s full-duplex. What will the outcome be when you plug in the node?
choices: The switch interface will be set to the 10 Mb/s full-duplex.
The switch interface will be set to the 100 Mb/s full-duplex.
The switch interface will be set to the 10 Mb/s half-duplex.
The switch interface will be set to the 100 Mb/s half-duplex.
questions.explanation: Cisco switches can auto-detect speed, so the speed sensed will be 100 Mb/s. However, if the switch cannot detect the speed, then it will fall back to 10 Mb/s. Duplex is decided upon bandwidth when IEEE auto- negotiation is turned off. If the speed is 10 Mb/s or 100 Mb/s, then the duplex will be half-duplex; otherwise it will be full-duplex on 1000 Mb/s links.
questions.topic: 2.3 Troubleshoot interface and cable issues (collisions, errors, duplex, speed)

questions.question: You plug a 100 Mb/s hub into a switch. What is the expected outcome?
choices: The switch interface will be set to the 10 Mb/s full-duplex.
The switch interface will be set to the 10 Mb/s half-duplex.
The switch interface will be set to the 100 Mb/s half-duplex.
The switch interface will be set to the 100 Mb/s full-duplex.
questions.explanation: Hubs do not participate in IEEE negotiation, and therefore the speed will be detected. However, since duplex cannot be negotiated, 10 Mb/s and 100 Mb/s connections will be half-duplex and 1000 Mb/s connections will be full-duplex.
questions.topic: 2.3 Troubleshoot interface and cable issues (collisions, errors, duplex, speed)

questions.question: You want to see a status of all speed and duplex negotiations for all interfaces. Which command would you use?
questions.explanation: The show interfaces status command will display the port number, description, connected status, VLAN, duplex, speed, and type of interface.
questions.topic: 2.3 Troubleshoot interface and cable issues (collisions, errors, duplex, speed)

questions.question: You are trying to reprovision a switch in a different part of your network. However, you still see the old VLANs configured from the old network. How can you rectify the problem?
choices: Type erase startup-config , confirm it, and reload.
Type clear vlan , confirm it, and reload.
Delete the vlan.dat , confirm it, and reload.
questions.explanation: The vlan.dat is the database for VLANs configured on a switch either manually or through VTP. It is persistent even if config.text (startup-config) is deleted. You must manually delete the vlan.dat .
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: Which VLAN is the default VLAN used to configure all switches from the factory?
questions.explanation: All switches are configured by default with all interfaces in VLAN 1. This simplifies configuration if the switch is to be used as a direct replacement for a hub since nothing needs to be configured.

questions.question: What is the normal range for VLANs before you must use extended VLAN IDs?
questions.explanation: The normal VLAN range is 1 through 1001 before you must use the extended VLAN range.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: Which is a benefit to converting a network from a flat layer 2 network to a routed layer 3 VLAN-enabled network?
choices: Flexibility of user management and design
Decreased number of broadcast domains for increased bandwidth
Reduced complexity of design and operations
Increased collision domains for increased bandwidth
questions.explanation: The flexibility of design for workgroups of people and the ongoing management of moving and adding people is a benefit of a routed VLAN- enabled network.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: You have created a VLAN for the Research department. Now you need to configure an interface on the switch for the newly created VLAN. Which command will configure the interface for the respective VLAN?
questions.explanation: When you’re configuring an interface for a VLAN, only the VLAN number can be used. The correct command is switchport access vlan 9 .

questions.question: You are installing a VoIP phone on the same interface as an existing computer. Which command will allow the VoIP phone to switch traffic onto its respective VLAN?
questions.explanation: The switchport voice vlan 4 command will configure the interface to switch traffic with a COS value of 5 set by the phone to the voice VLAN of 4.

questions.question: Which type of port removes the VLAN ID from the frame before it egresses the interface?
questions.explanation: All VLAN tagging is removed from the frame before it egresses an access port to the end device.

questions.question: You want to delete VLAN 1 for security reasons. However, the switch will not let you. What is the reason you cannot delete VLAN 1?
choices: The VLAN serves as the switch’s main management IP.
The VLAN is protected from deletion.
The VLAN is still configured on a port.
The VLAN is still configured as a native VLAN on a trunk.
questions.explanation: VLANs 1 and 1002 through 1005 are protected by the IOS and cannot be changed, renamed, or deleted.

questions.question: Which is a true statement about extended VLANs?
choices: You cannot configure extended VLANs until the normal VLANs are all used.
Extended VLANs are saved in the VLAN database.
VTP versions 1 and 2 require the switch to be in transparent mode.
Extended VLANs can only be used for FDDI.
questions.explanation: By default, the VTP mode is server. VTP v1 and v2 do not support storage and propagation of extended VLANs. However, when the switch is put into transparent mode, it does not participate in VTP, so the VLANs can be configured.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: What is the extended VLAN range?
questions.explanation: The extended VLAN range is VLAN 1006 to 4094.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: Why is it recommended that you do not use VLAN 1?
choices: It cannot be routed via an SVI.
It is not a production VLAN.
It shouldn’t be used for security reasons.
It cannot participate in VTP transfers.
questions.explanation: For security concerns, it should not be used in production. It is the default VLAN configured on all switches. Potentially, a computer can be plugged into an interface defaulted to VLAN 1 and expose resources such as the switch management network.

questions.question: You need to create a VLAN to support jumbo frames. Which commands would configure jumbo frame support on a VLAN?
questions.explanation: Configuration of jumbo frames requires creation of the VLAN from a global configuration prompt and then setting the maximum transmission unit (MTU). The value of the MTU will differ from switch to switch but is usually 9,000 bytes or higher.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: What is the command to verify a VLAN and the port(s) it is associated with?
questions.explanation: The command to verify that a VLAN is created and the port(s) it is associated with is show vlan .
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: Which command(s) will delete a VLAN?
questions.explanation: The command to delete VLAN 9 is no vlan 9 performed from a global configuration prompt.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: Which is a correct statement about frame and VLANs?
choices: Unicast frames that are not in the MAC address table are flooded to all ports in all VLANs.
Frames with a destination MAC that are not in the MAC address table are flooded to only ports in the respective VLAN.
The ports that link switches together must be access links.
Broadcast frames are sent to ports that are configured in different VLANs.
questions.explanation: Frames with MAC addresses that are not in the MAC address table are flooded only to the ports in the respective VLAN.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: A VLAN is not configured yet, but you mistakenly configure it on an interface via the command switch access vlan 12 . What will happen?
choices: The command will complete, but before forwarding can happen, the VLAN must be manually created.
The command will need to be negated and performed after the VLAN is manually created.
The command will complete and update the VLAN database.
questions.explanation: When the command is invoked inside of the interface, it will create the VLAN automatically.

questions.question: What is the normal range of VLANs that can be modified on a Cisco switch with default configuration?
questions.explanation: The normal range of VLANs on a default Cisco switch is VLAN 1 to 1001. However, VLAN 1 cannot be modified.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: Static VLANs are being used on a switch’s interface. Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: Nodes are assigned VLANs based on their MAC address.
Nodes use a VLAN policy server.
Nodes are unaware of the VLAN in which they are configured.
All nodes are in the same VLAN.
questions.explanation: Static VLANs are VLANs that have been manually configured vs. dynamic VLANs that are configured via a VLAN Membership Policy Server (VMPS). A node will not know which VLAN it is assigned to when it is statically set via the command switchport access vlan 3 .
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: A switch is configured with a single VLAN of 12 for all interfaces. All nodes auto-negotiate at 100 Mb/s full-duplex. What is true if you add an additional VLAN to the switch.
choices: The switch will increase its count of collision domains.
The switch will decrease its bandwidth due to overhead.
The switch will now require a router.
The switch will increase its bandwidth due to broadcast domains.
questions.explanation: The addition of another VLAN will increase the effective bandwidth by adding additional broadcast domains. A router is required to route between VLANs. However, it will not be required if you are logically partitioning the switch via VLANs.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: What is a direct benefit of adding VLANs?
choices: A decrease of broadcast domains while decreasing collision domains
An increase of broadcast domains while decreasing collision domains
A decrease of broadcast domains while increasing collisions domains
An increase of broadcast domains while increasing collision domains
questions.explanation: When adding VLANs, you immediately increase the number of broadcast domains. At the same time you increase collision domains. If a switch had 12 ports and they all negotiated at 100 Mb/s half-duplex (one collision domain), when a VLAN is added you will automatically create two collision domains while adding an additional broadcast domain.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: Which statement describes dynamic VLANs?
choices: The access port is switched into the respective VLAN based upon the computer’s IP address.
The access port is switched into the respective VLAN based upon user credentials.
The access port is switched into the respective VLAN based upon the computer’s MAC address.
The access port is switched into the respective VLAN based upon security ACLs.
questions.explanation: Dynamic VLANs are deprecated, but you may still see them in operations. A switch configured with dynamic VLANs checks a VLAN Management Policy Server (VMPS) when clients plug in. The VMPS has a list of MAC addresses to their respective VLANs. It is now recommended that dynamic VLAN installations are converted to 802.1x.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: You have changed the name of VLAN 3, and you now want to check your change. Which command will you enter to verify the name change?
questions.explanation: To verify a VLAN name change, you would use the command show vlan id 3 . This would only show you the one VLAN configured in the database. show vlans is incorrect because the command is not plural; it is singular, show vlan . It will give you a complete listing of all VLANs.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: You have been asked to segment the network for an R&D workgroup. The requirement is to allow the R&D group access to the existing servers, but no other VLANs should be able to access R&D. How can this be achieved with maximum flexibility?
choices: Create a new VLAN, and install a new R&D server in the new VLAN.
Create a new VLAN, configure a routed SVI interface, and apply ACLs to the R&D ports.
Create a new VLAN, and trunk the existing file server for both the production and R&D network.
Create a new VLAN, configure a routed SVI interface, and apply ACLs to the VLAN.
questions.explanation: Creating the new VLAN will logically segment this work group. Creating a Switched Virtual Interface (SVI) will allow routing on the layer 3 switch. The ACLs should only be applied to VLAN interfaces. Although the other solutions achieve a similar goal, they do not provide flexibility.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: You need to verify that an interface is in the proper VLAN. Which command will display the status of the interface, the VLAN configured, and the operational mode?
questions.explanation: The command show interfaces switchport will display a detail of all ports in respect to VLAN operational status. The command will show the operational mode of the interface, such as trunk or access mode.

questions.question: You configured VLAN on an interface, but it is not working. After looking at the VLAN database, you find it has been disabled. Which command will enable the VLAN?
questions.explanation: The proper way to enable a VLAN to forward traffic is to first enter the VLAN database for ID 3 and then issue the no shutdown command. On some IOS versions, this can also be done via the command no shutdown vlan 3 from global config mode.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: Which command will show the operational mode of only Fa0/3?
questions.explanation: The command show interfaces FastEthernet 0/3 switchport will show the switchport details for only Fa0/3, to include its operational mode. This command is similar to show interfaces switchport , which will show all ports.

questions.question: Which of the following is a true statement about static access ports?
choices: A client computer cannot see any VLAN tagging information.
A client computer can see the VLAN tagging information.
A client computer can request the VLAN to be placed in.
An access port can carry VLANs via tagging.
questions.explanation: The client computer connected to an access port cannot see any VLAN tagging information. It is removed before egress of the interface.

questions.question: Which of the following is a true statement, if you have changed the MTU on a VLAN to support jumbo frames?
choices: Once jumbo frames are configured, nothing more needs to be done. Clients will auto-detect the new MTU and use jumbo frames.
If a normal MTU of 1528 is used, the switch will not forward the traffic.
For jumbo frames to be effective, all devices on the VLAN, including switches, must support them.
Changing the MTU is an easy and effective method for raising speed.
questions.explanation: When the MTU is changed on the VLAN, it has little consequence to normal MTU communications. However, if you are going to utilize the new MTU for something like iSCSI, it must be supported end to end or it can actually decrease performance. All switching equipment between the two end devices must support jumbo frames.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: You have configured an access port for a remote office computer. The office has no IT persons on site. You want to stop workers from plugging in a WAP and exposing your company’s internal network. Which feature should you configure?
questions.explanation: Since the remote office has no onsite IT personnel, there is a risk of workers plugging in unauthorized equipment such as a WAP. If port security is implemented, the interface can be secured to allow only the MAC address of the computer to pass; all other traffic can be dropped.

questions.question: Which is a benefit of implementing routed VLANs?
choices: ACLs can be employed to secure VLANs.
Implementing routed VLANs will decrease the broadcast domains.
questions.explanation: When layer 3 or routed VLANs are implemented, it allows for a more secure network with the use of ACLs applied to the VLAN interface.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: You are running a wireless LAN controller (WLC) for a WLAN. You want to allow for guests to be segmented to the guest VLAN. What will you need to implement on the WLC?
choices: Access control lists for two SSIDs
Access control lists for one SSID
Two SSIDs, one configured to the production VLAN and another configured to the guest VLAN
questions.explanation: Wireless LAN controllers allow trunks to be used so that multiple VLANs can be used. Once the VLANs are accessible to the WLC, you need to create one SSID tied to the VLAN configured for production and another SSID tied to the VLAN configured for guests.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: What is the difference between a default VLAN and a native VLAN?
choices: A native VLAN is configured on all access ports of the switch from the factory.
A default VLAN is configured on all trunks for tagged frames.
A default VLAN is configured on all access ports of the switch from the factory.
A native VLAN is configured on all trunks for tagged frames.
questions.explanation: The default VLAN for all switches is VLAN 1. It is the default configuration for all access ports from the factory.

questions.question: Where is the extended VLAN configuration stored?
questions.explanation: The extended VLAN database will be stored in the startup-config. Only normal VLANs are stored in the VLAN database ( vlan.dat ). When configuring extended VLANs, you must have the switch in VTP transparent mode.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: You need to create a new VLAN 5 called office and apply it to interface Fa0/4. Which commands will you need to enter?
choices: Switch(config)#vlan 5 Switch(config-vlan)#name office Switch(config-vlan)#exit Switch(config)#interface fast 0/4 Switch(config-if)#switchport access vlan office
Switch(config)#vlan 5 name office Switch(config)#interface fast 0/4 Switch(config-if)#switchport access vlan 5
Switch(config)#vlan 5 Switch(config-vlan)#name office Switch(config-vlan)#exit Switch(config)#interface fast 0/4 Switch(config-if)#switchport access vlan 5
Switch(config)#vlan 5 office Switch(config)#interface fast 0/4 Switch(config-if)#switchport access vlan 5
questions.explanation: You should first create the VLAN in the VLAN database and add its name. Then you need to enter the interface and configure the port for the VLAN.

questions.question: A VLAN was created on another non-Cisco switch. You look at the current VLAN database, but the VLAN is not in the VLAN database. What must be done to correct the issue?
choices: Set the correct trunking protocol between the switches.
Assign the VLAN to an interface on the other switch.
questions.explanation: You must manually configure the VLAN on the Cisco switch(s). VTP is a protocol that allows for VLAN autoconfiguration in the VLAN database. However, only Cisco switches support it.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: Which command(s) will rename an existing VLAN 4 from production to office without interruption to the network?
questions.explanation: In global configuration, you first need to enter the entry of the VLAN in the VLAN database. Then you can issue a name command to overwrite the existing entry. Negating the VLAN 4 and re-creating it would also work but would create interruption when it was destroyed.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: You have been tasked to configure an interface with a VLAN ID of 8 and support a VoIP phone on VLAN 6. Which commands would achieve the goal?
choices: Switch(config-if)#switchport mode access vlan 8 Switch(config-if)#switchport voice vlan 6
Switch(config-if)#switchport access vlan 8 Switch(config-if)#switchport voice vlan 6
questions.explanation: The command used to configure an access port for VLAN 8 is switchport access vlan 8 , and the command to configure the VOIP phone is switchport voice vlan 6 .

questions.question: You attempt to configure a VLAN on a switch of VLAN 2300. When you finish configuring the VLAN and exit the VLAN database, you receive the error “% Failed to create VLANS 2300.” What is wrong?
choices: The VLAN database cannot be configured for VLAN 2300.
The VLAN database is too large and out of space.
The VTP mode must be transparent to configure VLAN 2300.
The VLAN must be configured on an interface first.
questions.explanation: One of the prerequisites for configuring extended VLANs is that the VTP mode must be transparent.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: You attempt to configure a VLAN with a new name. You receive the error “Default VLAN 1 may not have its name changed.” What is wrong?
choices: You are not in the VLAN database when committing the change.
The VLAN is used on interfaces already.
The VLAN is being referenced by its name in interface configuration.
The VLAN is protected from any changes.
questions.explanation: VLAN 1 is the default VLAN and it is not permitted by the IOS to change the VLAN in any way. This includes name changes.

questions.question: You have configured a VLAN for an MTU of 9128. However, you have noticed a severe performance decrease from the change. What is the problem?
choices: The device does not support jumbo frames.
One of the connected switches is still configured for a nominal MTU.
The VLAN configuration must still propagate to the other switches.
The VTP protocol is not configured correctly.
questions.explanation: Although the MTU is configured on the VLAN, all switches and devices connected end to end must be configured to support jumbo frames. If you fail to do this, you can expect to see a performance decrease. An MTU of 9128 is defined as a jumbo frame.
questions.topic: 2.4 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot VLANs (normal/extended range) spanning multiple switches

questions.question: You have connected a Dell switch to the Cisco switch you are configuring and you cannot get a trunk between the two. What must be changed?
choices: VTP needs to be configured on each of the switches.
The Dell switch must be configured to use ISL.
The Cisco switch must be configured to use 802.1Q.
Both switches need to have duplicated VLAN configurations.
questions.explanation: Since the Dell switch cannot support the proprietary protocol of ISL, both switches need to be set up to use 802.1Q.

questions.question: You need to configure a trunk interface to support the protocol of 802.1Q. Which command will achieve this?
questions.explanation: The command to specify 802.1Q encapsulation on a trunk interface is switchport trunk encapsulation 802.1q .

questions.question: You are trying to configure a trunk port on an interface for 802.1Q encapsulation. However, after entering the proper command, you receive the error % Invalid input detected at '^' marker. What is wrong?
choices: The switch only supports the ISL trunking protocol.
802.1Q is not supported on the switch you are configuring this on.
The interface will not allow configuration of 802.1Q.
The switch only supports the 802.1Q trunking protocol.
questions.explanation: This error is very common when configuring Cisco switches, since many switches only support 802.1Q and configuration is not necessary. The ISL trunking protocol is not supported on certain platforms, such as the 2900 series switches.

questions.question: You need to view all of the trunks on a switch and verify that they have the proper trunking protocols configured. Which command will display the information?
questions.explanation: The command show interfaces trunk will display all of the configured trunks on the switch.

questions.question: When a frame is not tagged with 802.1Q VLAN identifying information, what happens when it traverses a trunk port?
choices: The frame is forwarded to the native VLAN.
The frame is sent to the first VLAN ID configured on the trunk.
The frame is forwarded to the default VLAN.
The frame is dropped to the bit bucket.
questions.explanation: When a frame traverses a trunk and does not have VLAN tagging information in the 802.1Q encapsulation format (untagged), it is sent to the native VLAN configured on the trunk.

questions.question: What is the default VTP mode all switches are configured as by default?
questions.explanation: All switches are configured by default as a VTP server.

questions.question: You need to verify the VTP mode on a switch. Which command will display the information?
questions.explanation: The command to display the mode settings for VTP is show vtp status .

questions.question: Which commands would you enter on a new switch joining your existing network to configure VTP?
choices: Switch(config)#vtp mode client Switch(config)#vtp domain corpname
Switch(config)#vtp mode transparent Switch(config)#vtp domain corpname
questions.explanation: When setting up VTP on a new switch connected to your existing VTP infrastructure, you need to change the mode of the switch. Then you must configure the VTP domain that is serving the VTP information.

questions.question: Which protocol is an open standard trunking protocol?
questions.explanation: The 802.1Q protocol is supported by all switches’ vendors for trunking. It is an open standard that was developed by the IEEE.

questions.question: Which command will show you the native VLAN for only Fa0/15?
questions.explanation: The command show interface fastethernet 0/15 switchport will show the operational mode, and if configured as a trunk, it will show the native VLAN.

questions.question: You need to change the native VLAN for interface Fa0/23 from VLAN 1 to VLAN 999. Which command would you use?
choices: Switch(config-if)#no switchport native vlan 1 Switch(config-if)#switchport native vlan 999
questions.explanation: The command to change the native VLAN of a trunk to VLAN 999 is switchport trunk native vlan 999 .

questions.question: When you change the native VLAN of a trunk from VLAN 1 to VLAN 999 and you receive the error “%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered…,” what is the possible problem?
choices: The version of CDP is wrong on the other switch.
The interface is the first to be changed.
CDP is not running on the other interface, causing a mismatch.
questions.explanation: This error is normal if it is the first interface to be changed over to the new native VLAN since the other interface has not been changed yet. However, if the other interface was changed already and you received this error, then CDP is letting you know that the other side is mismatched.

questions.question: Which command will turn off Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP) on an interface?
questions.explanation: The Dynamic Trunking Protocol can be turned off with the command switchport nonegotiate , which when configured states not to negotiate trunks via DTP.

questions.question: You need to remove VLANs 2 through 4 from the allowed list on a trunk interface. Which command will remove only these VLANs without interruption to the network?
questions.explanation: The command switchport trunk allowed vlan remove 2-4 will remove VLANs 2 through 4 from the trunk.
questions.topic: 2.5b Add and remove VLANs on a trunk

questions.question: You are trunking Switch A and Switch B together. On Switch A you have the default of switchport mode dynamic auto . On Switch B, which command will you need to configure to allow trunking?
questions.explanation: Switch B will need to either have its interface set to switchport mode trunk or switchport mode dynamic desirable for Switch A to turn its interface into a trunk.

questions.question: You need to add VLAN 4 to the allowed list on a trunk interface. Currently VLANs 5 through 8 are allowed. Which command will add only this VLAN without interruption to the network?
questions.explanation: The command switchport trunk allowed vlan add 4 will add VLAN 4 to the existing list of VLANs already allowed on the interface.
questions.topic: 2.5b Add and remove VLANs on a trunk

questions.question: You try to configure the command switchport mode trunk on an interface. However, you see the error message “Command rejected: An interface whose trunk encapsulation is Auto cannot be configured to trunk mode.” What command will fix the issue?
questions.explanation: The command will not complete because the interface is set to dynamic auto , which implies the trunk protocol will be negotiated. You cannot set it to switchport mode trunk until you statically set the encapsulation via the command switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q .

questions.question: What is the function of the VLAN Trunking Protocol (VTP)?
choices: VTP allows for propagation of the VLAN database.
VTP allows for propagation of the trunking database.
VTP detects trunks encapsulations and negotiates trunks.
VTP allows for dynamic trunking between links.
questions.explanation: VLAN Trunking Protocol, or VTP, propagates the VLAN database from an initial master copy on the “server” to all of the “clients.”

questions.question: Which protocol is a Cisco proprietary protocol used for trunking switches?
questions.explanation: Inter-Switch Link, or ISL, is a proprietary protocol used for trunking of switches. If you need to connect non-Cisco switches to a Cisco switch, you must use 802.1Q, the IEEE standard.

questions.question: How does IEEE 802.1Q tag frames?
choices: 802.1Q adds a 32-bit header to the packet with the VLAN tagging information.
802.1Q inserts a 32-bit field between the destination MAC address and the type field.
802.1Q adds a 32-bit header to the frame with the VLAN tagging information.
802.1Q inserts a 32-bit field between the source MAC address and the type field.
questions.explanation: 802.1Q inserts a field containing the 16-bit Tag Protocol ID of 0x8100, a 3-bit COS field, a 1-bit drop-eligible indicator (used with COS), and the 12=bit VLAN ID, which equals 32 bits, or 4 bytes.

questions.question: Which VTP mode will not allow the switch to participate in VTP traffic but will forward VTP traffic?
questions.explanation: A switch in VTP transparent mode will not participate in VTP. However, if the VTP is v2, the switch will forward and receive VTP advertisements.

questions.question: Which commands will allow a trunk with another switch configured as mode desirable auto?
choices: SwitchB(config-if)#switchport mode dynamic auto SwitchB(config-if)#switchport mode encapsulation dot1q
SwitchB(config-if)#switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q SwitchB(config-if)#switchport mode trunk
SwitchB(config-if)#switchport encapsulation dot1q SwitchB(config-if)#switchport mode trunk
questions.explanation: You must first set the encapsulation to 802.1Q, then you can statically set the mode to trunk. An alternative would be to set the port to dynamic desirable via the command switchport mode dynamic desirable . However, it is recommended to statically configure the link to trunk on one or both sides if possible.

questions.question: What significance does VTP VLAN pruning provide?
choices: VLAN pruning removes VLAN traffic from other switches that are not configured for the respective VLAN.
VLAN pruning removes VLANs from the databases of other switches that they are not configured on.
VLAN pruning automatically changes the allowed VLANs on all interfaces.
questions.explanation: VTP VLAN pruning removes forwarding traffic for VLANs that are not configured on remote switches. This saves bandwidth on trunks because if the remote switch does not have the VLAN configured on it, the frame destined for the VLAN will not traverse the trunk.

questions.question: Which command enables VTP pruning?
questions.explanation: The command “ vtp pruning in global configuration mode will enable VTP VLAN pruning.

questions.question: Switch A and Switch B have a trunk. On Switch A, the native VLAN is set to VLAN 10 on Switch B and the native VLAN is defaulted. What problems will occur?
choices: Any traffic not tagged on Switch B when traversing the trunk will be switched onto VLAN 10.
All broadcasts will be forwarded to Switch B.
questions.explanation: The problems will not be apparent since the trunk will still function for tagged traffic. However, any traffic that is not tagged will be directed to the opposite side’s native VLAN. So traffic expected for VLAN 1 will be directed to VLAN 10, and VLAN 10 traffic will be directed to VLAN 1 when not tagged.

questions.question: When enabling VTP pruning, where does it need to be configured?
choices: VTP needs to be configured only on the VTP server.
VTP needs to be configured on all VTP clients and the server.
VTP needs to be configured only on the VTP transparent.
VTP needs to be configured only on the VTP client.
questions.explanation: VTP pruning needs to be configured only on the VTP server. The clients will receive the update and turn on VTP pruning automatically.

questions.question: Which proprietary protocol allows for conformity of VLANs across all Cisco switches?
questions.explanation: VLAN Trunking Protocol allows for conformity of VLANs across all Cisco switches. The protocol uses a master-slave database with a revision control of +1. If the server is 5 and the clients are 4, they will update the database to the latest revision.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about native VLANs?
choices: Any traffic tagged will be placed on the native VLAN.
Any traffic that is not allowed over the trunk will be placed on the native VLAN.
Any traffic that is tagged with ISL on an 802.1Q trunk will be placed on the native VLAN.
Any traffic not tagged will be placed on the native VLAN.
questions.explanation: Native VLANs are only used for traffic that is not tagged, which is placed on a trunk link. A common use for native VLANs is management traffic between switches, before both sides are configured as a trunk.

questions.question: You have configured switchport nonegotiate on an interface with a default configuration. What effect will it have on the neighboring interface when the other switch is plugged in with its interface in default configuration?
choices: The switchport will transition to a trunk port.
The interface will remain shut down.
The switchport will remain an access port.
The interface will enter an err-disable state.
questions.explanation: If you issue the command switchport nonegotiate , the switch will not send Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP) frames for trunk negotiation. The default configuration for a port is the mode of access, so the port will remain in an access port.

questions.question: Switch A has the default configuration on its interface. You plug Switch B into its interface with a crossover cable. Which command will force Switch B to become a member of VLAN 5?
choices: SwitchB(config-if)#switchport mode access SwitchB(config-if)#switchport access vlan 5
SwitchB(config-if)#switchport mode trunk SwitchB(config-if)#switchport native vlan 5
SwitchA(config-if)#switchport mode access SwitchA(config-if)#switchport access vlan 5
SwitchA(config-if)#switchport mode trunk SwitchA(config-if)#switchport native vlan 5
questions.explanation: You want Switch B to become a member of VLAN 5. So Switch A must change its interface to an access port, which will force Switch B to remain an access port. Then you configure the access VLAN of 5 on Switch A. If you tried to configure this with a native VLAN, you would result in a native VLAN mismatch and improper configuration.

questions.question: Switch A is configured with the command of switchport mode dynamic desirable on its interface. Which command would you need to configure on Switch B to create a trunk between them?
questions.explanation: The command switchport mode dynamic desirable is similar to switchport mode dynamic auto with the exception that it is desirable to become a trunk. So if the neighboring port is set to auto, desirable, or trunk, it becomes a trunk.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about the command switchport mode dynamic auto ?
choices: The interface will remain an access link if the neighboring port is configured as a trunk.
The interface will remain an access link if the native VLAN is changed.
The interface will become a trunk if the neighboring port is configured the same.
The interface will become a trunk if requested on the neighboring port.
questions.explanation: The command switchport mode dynamic auto will cause the port to remain an access port if the neighboring port is configured the same. However, if you configure the neighboring port as a trunk, it will become a trunk.

questions.question: Which command is similar to show interfaces trunk but will show greater detail?
questions.explanation: The command show interfaces switchport will show greater detail about the trunk than the command show interfaces trunk . Alternatively, you can specify a single port using the command show interfaces Fa 0/5 switchport , for example.

questions.question: You are connecting a VMware ESXi server to an interface on a 3560 switch. The ESXi server will need several VLANs for the VMs running on it. How would you configure the interface?
choices: Switch(config-if)#switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q Switch(config-if)#switchport trunk Switch(config-if)#switchport nonegotiate
Switch(config-if)#switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q Switch(config-if)#switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)#switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q Switch(config-if)#switchport mode dynamic desirable
Switch(config-if)#switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q Switch(config-if)#switchport mode trunk Switch(config-if)#switchport nonegotiate
questions.explanation: Configuring servers like VMware ESXi is no different than configuring other switches. The exception is that the VMware server will not participate in DTP. So we first configure the command to set the interface statically to a trunk. Then we turn off DTP with the command switchport nonegotiate since DTP is not needed.

questions.question: When you have a native VLAN mismatch on a configured trunk, which protocol will alert you to the issue?
questions.explanation: Cisco Discovery Protocol (CDP) will alert you to a native VLAN mismatch. You will receive the error “%CDP-4- NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered….” When a trunk is configured, the native VLAN is always used for CDP exchanges.

questions.question: How does a VTP client know that the VTP database has been updated?
choices: The CDP protocol checks for VTP updates.
The VTP protocol checks the MD5 checksum for changes.
The VTP protocol pulls a full copy of the database every 60 seconds.
The VTP protocol checks the database revision number.
questions.explanation: The VTP clients track changes via a 32-bit number inside of the VTP frame called the revision number. By default, every 5 minutes a summary advertisement is sent from the server. However, when an update occurs, a new VTP frame called a subset advert message is sent.

questions.question: What can happen by changing the mode of a VTP client to a VTP server and changing one of the VLANs?
choices: The VLAN database can be overwritten in the rest of the network.
Nothing; the switch functions fine in the rest of the network.
The VLAN database can be erased in the rest of the network.
The switch will need to be reloaded before it can function as a server.
questions.explanation: Since the VTP clients in the network check the revision number in VTP, if a client is changed to a server, the database remains intact. So when a change is made, the revision number will increment and propagate to the rest of the network. Even if an existing server exists, its revision number will be lower.

questions.question: You need to check the allowed VLANs on a trunk interface. Which command will show you the allowed VLANs?
questions.explanation: The command show interfaces trunk will show the details of allowed VLANs. The show running-config command will also show you the allowed VLANs.
questions.topic: 2.5b Add and remove VLANs on a trunk

questions.question: You need to verify if VTP pruning is enabled. Which command will you use to view the information?
questions.explanation: The command show vtp status will tell you if VTP pruning is enabled or disabled.

questions.question: You are trying to change the native VLAN from VLAN 1 to VLAN 1002. You have configured both sides with switchport native vlan 1002 . However, the native VLAN traffic keeps failing. What is wrong?
choices: VLAN 1002 is not allowed for Ethernet traffic.
The native VLAN must be VLAN 1.
The native VLAN cannot be an extended VLAN.
The problem is not the native VLAN; everything is configured properly.
questions.explanation: VLAN 1002 is reserved for use with an FDDI VLAN and not allowed for Ethernet traffic. All Ethernet traffic must be a VLAN between 1 to 1001. You cannot use 1002 to 1005 because they are used for legacy applications.

questions.question: What is the IEEE specification for Spanning Tree Protocol?
questions.explanation: The original version of STP was created by Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC). The IEEE ratified the specification of STP as 802.1d in 1990.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: Which statement is correct about Spanning Tree Protocol?
choices: STP runs as a distributed process on each switch and creates a topology database.
STP uses routing protocols to check for network loops.
STP runs on a central switch by creating a topology database.
STP uses the MAC address table to check for switching loops.
questions.explanation: Spanning Tree Protocol runs as a distributed process on each switch. Each switch creates and maintains its own topology database referencing the root bridge.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: How does Spanning Tree Protocol detect and monitor loops in networks?
choices: STP detects and monitors CDP frames being received on multiple interfaces.
STP detects and monitors BPDUs being received on multiple interfaces.
STP detects and monitors access ports in the same VLAN.
STP detects and monitors normal traffic frames being received on multiple interfaces.
questions.explanation: STP monitors all interfaces for BPDUs, which carry switches’ identities. When it sees the same switch ID in BPDUs on multiple interfaces, a redundant link is detected.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: How is the root bridge in STP elected?
choices: The root bridge is the switch with the lowest MAC address and priority.
The root bridge is the switch with the lowest IP address and priority.
The root bridge is the switch with the highest MAC address and priority.
The root bridge is the switch with the highest IP address and priority.
questions.explanation: The root bridge is elected by all of the switches and has the lowest MAC address and priority of them all.

questions.question: What is the IEEE specification for Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol?
questions.explanation: The original STP specification was revamped in 2004 with RSTP 802.1w. This revamping of STP was to fix problems with the original specification.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: Why is a root bridge elected for STP to function properly?
choices: The root bridge calculates the port cost for the rest of the network.
The root bridge calculates the fastest path for the rest of the network.
The root bridge is the logical center of the STP topology.
The root bridge allows all forwarding decisions of frames.
questions.explanation: The root bridge is a point of perspective for the rest of the STP network. It is important to have a point of perspective to calculate which ports are blocked and which remain in a forwarding mode.

questions.question: How does a switch calculate the bridge ID?
choices: The bridge ID is an 8-byte number containing a 4-byte bridge priority and 4-byte IP address.
The bridge ID is a 6-byte number containing a 2-byte bridge priority and 4-byte IP address.
The bridge ID is a 10-byte number containing a 4-byte bridge priority and 6-byte MAC address.
The bridge ID is an 8-byte number containing a 2-byte bridge priority and 6-byte MAC address.
questions.explanation: The bridge ID is made up of a 2-byte bridge priority and a 6-byte MAC address for a total of 8 bytes.

questions.question: What is the link cost in respect to STP?
choices: Link cost is the calculation of all the ports in the path to the root bridge.
Link cost is the monetary cost to traverse a link.
Link cost is the latency of a frame traversing across the link.
Link cost is a numeric value associated with the speed of a link.
questions.explanation: The link cost is a numeric value that represents the cost in speed of a link. The higher the numbers, the lower the speed of the link, thus a higher cost.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: What is the path cost in respect to RSTP?
choices: Path cost is a numeric value associated with the speed of a link.
Path cost is the latency of a frame traversing across the link.
Path cost is the calculation of all the ports in the path to the root bridge.
Path cost is the monetary cost to traverse a link.
questions.explanation: The RSTP path cost is the calculation of all of the link costs that lead back to the root bridge. The link cost is a numeric value that signifies the speed. The lower the number “cost,” the higher the speed of the link.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: What is the default wait time for STP convergence to complete?
questions.explanation: 802.1d STP convergence takes 50 seconds to complete before the port is put into a state of forwarding or blocking. This is dependent on the STA, or spanning-tree algorithm.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: When a computer is connected to an interface with STP enabled in default mode, which is the correct order of the port transitions?
questions.explanation: When a computer is connected to an STP-enabled interface, the port will transition between blocking, listening, learning, and forwarding. The time between the states of blocking and forwarding is called the convergence and is 50 seconds.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: What is the definition of a designated port?
choices: A port that is determined to have a lowest path cost to the root bridge and placed in a forwarding state for a network segment
A port that is determined to have the highest cost and placed in a forwarding state for a network segment
A port that is determined to have the highest path cost to the root bridge and placed in a blocking state for a network segment
A port that is determined to have the lowest cost and placed in a forwarding state for a network segment
questions.explanation: A designated port is a port that has the lowest cost compared to the higher cost of the redundant ports. It is placed into a forwarding state for a network segment.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: Which is a correct statement about bridge port roles in STP?
choices: Every switch, including the root bridge, must have at least one backup port.
Every switch, excluding the root bridge, must have at least one root port.
Every switch, excluding the root bridge, must have at least one alternate port.
Every switch, including the root bridge, must have at least one designated port.
questions.explanation: Every switch in the network segment must have at least one root port. This is the port that leads back to the root bridge. The root bridge will have a designated port on the adjacent link.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: What is the definition of an STP root port?
choices: A port that is determined to have the highest path cost to the root bridge and placed in a blocking state for a network segment
A port that is determined to have the highest cost to the network segment and placed in a forwarding state
A port that is determined to have the lowest path cost to the root bridge and placed in a forwarding state for a network segment
A port that is determined to have the lowest cost to the network segment and placed in a forwarding state
questions.explanation: The root port is the port that leads back to the root bridge on the adjacent switch. It has the lowest cost of the redundant ports.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: Which statement describes an STP port that is placed into a blocking state?
choices: When a port is placed into a blocking state, it blocks redundant frames, including BPDUs.
When a port is placed into a blocking state, it blocks redundant frames, excluding BPDUs.
When a port is placed into a blocking state, it blocks all frames, including BPDUs.
When a port is placed into a blocking state, it blocks all frames, excluding BPDUs.
questions.explanation: An STP blocked port will block all frames from being forwarded. The blocking excludes BPDUs, which it will continue to listen for and calculate future topology decisions.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: Which protocol is a Cisco proprietary enhancement for 802.1d that allows separate spanning-tree instances for each VLAN?
questions.explanation: Per-VLAN Spanning Tree+ elects a root bridge for each VLAN and creates a topology table for each VLAN. It is a Cisco proprietary protocol due to the bridge ID calculation it must perform for each VLAN.

questions.question: What is the definition of an STP designated port?
choices: A port that is determined to have the highest cost to the network segment and placed in a forwarding state
A port that is determined to have the lowest cost to the network segment and placed in a forwarding state
A port that is determined to have the lowest path cost to the root bridge and placed in a forwarding state for a network segment
A port that is determined to have the highest path cost to the root bridge and placed in a blocking state for a network segment
questions.explanation: The designated port is the port with the lowest cost of the redundant links to the network segment. The adjacent port is normally the root port leading back to the root bridge.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: When a computer is connected to an interface with RSTP enabled in default mode, which is the correct order of the port transitions?
questions.explanation: RSTP has three transitions when a computer is plugged in (no loops). The transitions are discarding, learning, and forwarding, which allow for rapid convergence times.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: How is the bridge ID calculated for PVST+?
choices: The bridge ID is a 4-bit bridge priority, 12-bit sys-id-ext, and an 8- byte IP address.
The bridge ID is a 4-byte bridge priority and sys-id-ext and 6-byte MAC address.
The bridge ID is a 4-byte bridge priority, a 12-byte sys-id-ext, and 6 byte MAC address.
The bridge ID is a 4-bit bridge priority, 12-bit sys-id-ext, and 6-byte MAC address.
questions.explanation: The PVST+ bridge ID comprises a 4-bit bridge priority calculated in blocks of 4096, a 12-bit sys-ext-id that is the VLAN ID for the segment, and a 6-byte MAC address for the switch.

questions.question: What is the default bridge priority for all STP switches?
questions.explanation: The default bridge priority for STP is 32,768.

questions.question: Which protocol is a Cisco proprietary enhancement for 802.1w that allows separate spanning-tree instances for each VLAN?
questions.explanation: Rapid Per-VLAN Spanning Tree+ elects a root bridge for each VLAN. It allows for fast convergence times and logical placement of the root bridge. However, it requires the most CPU and RAM of all implementations.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about the Common Spanning Tree?
choices: CST is best implemented for really large networks since it scales efficiently.
CST elects a single root bridge for the entire physical network.
CST has an immediate convergence because it elects a single root bridge.
CST elects a root bridge for each VLAN.
questions.explanation: Common Spanning Tree elects a single root bridge for the entire network and all of the VLANs. This creates a problem when the center of your network may vary upon VLAN placement.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: Which statement is correct about Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol?
choices: RSTP has a convergence time of around 50 seconds.
RSTP allows for multiple root bridges.
RSTP is backward compatible with STP.
RSTP has five port states to which the interfaces could possibly transition.
questions.explanation: RSTP has three transition modes and converges faster than STP, which is 50 seconds. It is, however, backward compatible with STP 802.1d.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: How do switches participating in an STP network become aware of topology changes?
choices: Each switch is responsible for sensing the change and sending Topology Change Notification BPDUs.
The root bridge polls each switch participating in STP for changes.
The root bridge is responsible for sensing the change and sending Topology Change Notification BPDUs.
The switches participating in STP poll the root bridge for changes.
questions.explanation: Each switch is responsible for sensing changes to the topology. Whenever the topology changes, a Topology Change Notification (TCN) is sent out all root ports and an acknowledgment is sent back. This happens until the root bridge sends back a notification.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: Which of the following standards is an IEEE standard that is to replace Rapid PVST+?
questions.explanation: 802.1s, which is called Multiple Spanning Tree (MST), is a standard based upon PVST+. It is an open standard created by the IEEE that will allow Per-VLAN Spanning Tree in multi-vendor switched networks. However, it is not fully supported on all Cisco platforms as of yet.

questions.question: Which is a correct statement about bridge port roles in STP?
choices: All ports on the root bridge are in a designated port state.
Every switch, excluding the root bridge, must have at least one non- designated port.
Every switch, including the root bridge, must have at least one designated port.
A designated port is always in a blocking state.
questions.explanation: The root bridge always has all of its ports in a designated mode or forwarding mode. If there are redundant links, the adjacent switch to the designated port on the root bridge must be a non-designated or blocking state.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: In Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol, which port mode replaces the blocking and listening port states?
questions.explanation: RSTP has three port states: discarding, learning, and forwarding. Blocking and listening are both mapped to discarding in RSTP. When a port is in a state of discarding, it means the interface is discarding all frames except for BPDUs.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: You have a network consisting of four switches, all configured with the same bridge priority. Which switch will be elected the root bridge?
questions.explanation: The switch with the MAC address of 0011.03ae.d8aa will become the root bridge. Its MAC address is the lowest out of the four switches.

questions.question: What is the default STP mode all Cisco switches run?
questions.explanation: All Cisco switches are defaulted to the Cisco proprietary STP protocol of PVST+.

questions.question: Which option is a correct statement about alternate ports in RSTP?
choices: An alternate port receives BDPUs from another port on the same switch and therefore can replace the designated port if it fails.
An alternate port receives BPDUs from another switch and therefore can replace the root port if it fails.
An alternate port is always placed in a forwarding state.
An alternate port receives BPDUs from another switch and therefore can replace the designated port if it fails.
questions.explanation: An alternate port is a port that is in a discarding state. If the root port fails on the switch with the alternate port, then the alternate port becomes the root port for that switch.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: Which is a correct statement about backup ports in RSTP?
choices: A backup port receives BPDUs from another switch and therefore can replace the root port if it fails.
A backup port is always placed in a forwarding state.
A backup port receives BDPUs from another port on the same switch and therefore can replace the designated port if it fails.
A backup port receives BPDUs from another switch and therefore can replace the designated port if it fails.
questions.explanation: A backup port is a port in a discarding state. It receives BPDUs from another port on the same switch. If the forwarding port fails, then the backup port will become designated so that connectivity to the segment can be restored.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: You have a network consisting of four switches. Which switch will be elected the root bridge?
questions.explanation: Although 00f8.034e.bede is the highest MAC address of the four switches, the priority is the lowest of the four. Since the priority and MAC address are added together, the priority allows the switch to win the election.

questions.question: Which command would configure the priority of 16,384 for VLAN 5?
