questions.explanation: The command to set the STP priority for VLAN 5 is performed from a global config prompt. The full command is spanning-tree vlan 5 priority 16384 .

questions.question: Which command will display the VLANs for which the current switch is the root bridge?
questions.explanation: The command show spanning-tree summary will show all of the VLANs for which the current switch is a root bridge.

questions.question: Which command will enable Rapid Per-VLAN Spanning Tree on a switch?
questions.explanation: Enabling Rapid PVST is super simple. From a global config prompt you use the command spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst .

questions.question: You want to see the spanning tree for one VLAN. Which command would you use?
questions.explanation: The command show spanning-tree vlan 6 would only show the spanning-tree configuration for VLAN 6.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: Which new port state does RTSP have compared to STP?
questions.explanation: The new port state that RTSP has is discarding, which replaces the blocking state of STP.
questions.topic: 2.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP protocols

questions.question: You receive a call that when computers boot up, they display an error message stating that they cannot reach a domain controller. However, after a few tries, the problem goes away, and the domain controller can be reached. Which command would you enter into the interface if you suspect spanning-tree convergence problems?
questions.explanation: The command spanning-tree portfast” entered into the interface will turn on PortFast mode. This will allow the interface to forward first.

questions.question: On which types of ports should you turn on PortFast mode?
questions.explanation: PortFast should only be configured on access links where end devices are plugged in because these devices will not typically create loops in the switch topology.

questions.question: What will the command of spanning-tree portfast default entered in global configuration mode do?
choices: Turn off spanning tree on all access ports only.
Turn on PortFast mode for all access ports only.
Turn on PortFast mode for all ports.
Turn off spanning tree on all ports.
questions.explanation: This command turns on PortFast globally for only access ports on the switch. This command should be used on access switches because end devices are connected at this level in the hierarchy.

questions.question: What will happen if you plug a hub into two ports on the same switch configured with PortFast on all the interfaces?
choices: One of the links will disable via spanning tree.
You will create a temporary switching loop.
Both ports will sense the switch and err-disable.
You will create a switching loop.
questions.explanation: You will create a temporary switching loop until the BPDUs are heard from each interface over the hub. However, during this period you will have a switching loop and degrade traffic over the entire switching topology until convergence happens.

questions.question: Which feature will protect a switch immediately if it sees another switch’s advertisement?
questions.explanation: BPDU Guard will turn the interface to err-disable as soon as a BPDU is heard on the interface. This feature should be enabled on access switches when configuring PortFast.

questions.question: What is the transition of states when PortFast is configured?
questions.explanation: PortFast mode allows an interface to bypass the blocking state and begin forwarding immediately. It then listens and learns of BPDUs on the interface and can make a decision to continue to forward frames or enter into a blocking state.

questions.question: Which command would you use to configure BPDU Guard on an interface?
questions.explanation: The correct command to configure BPDU Guard on a single interface is spanning-tree bpduguard entered into the interface you want to turn it on for.

questions.question: After you configure an access switch on your network, you receive a call that the users have lost connectivity. You examine the trunk interface with the command show interfaces Gi 0/1 . What might be the problem?
choices: The switch uplink cable is bad.
BPDU Guard was configured on a trunk.
A spanning-tree loop has been detected.
questions.explanation: BPDU Guard was turned on the trunk link. When the BPDU of the adjacent switch was seen, the switch turned the port into err-disabled mode.

questions.question: Which option is a best practice when configuring links on an access switch?
choices: Always configure BPDU Guard along with UplinkFast.
Never configure spanning-tree PortFast mode on an access link.
Always configure BPDU Guard on trunks.
Always configure BPDU Guard along with PortFast.
questions.explanation: Configuring BPDU Guard along with PortFast ensures that the end device will always be forwarding. BPDU Guard ensures that in the event a BPDU is heard on the interface, the interface will enter into an err-disable mode.
questions.topic: 2.7 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot STP related optional features

questions.question: Which command will show you if a port has been configured for PortFast mode?
questions.explanation: Using the command show spanning-tree interface fa 0/1 will show the spanning tree configuration for an interface. If PortFast has been configured, the last line will read, “The port is in the PortFast mode.”

questions.question: Which command would you use to remove BPDU Guard from an interface?
questions.explanation: One way to disable BDPU Guard is to enter the command spanning-tree bpduguard disable . Another way is to negate the command with no spanning-tree bpduguard .

questions.question: You have BPDU Guard configured on an interface. What happens if a BPDU is advertised on the interface?
choices: A small switching loop will happen until convergence.
The interface will become administratively disabled.
questions.explanation: The switch’s interface will become err-disabled immediately. Once it is in err-disable mode, an administrator is required to reset the interface.

questions.question: Which command will show you if BPDU Guard is enabled by default?
questions.explanation: The show spanning-tree summary command will show you which features are turned on globally or by default.

questions.question: You are configuring an edge switch and want to make sure that someone does not plug a switch in accidentally. Which feature will you configure?
questions.explanation: BPDU Guard will protect the edge switch from someone accidentally plugging in another switch to a port dedicated for end devices.

questions.question: You want to quickly configure an edge switch so all access ports are in PortFast mode. Which command will achieve this?
questions.explanation: The command spanning-tree portfast default will configure all access ports on the switch as PortFast enabled.

questions.question: Which protocol is an IEEE standard that collects information from neighboring devices on their identity and capabilities?
questions.explanation: Link Layer Discovery Protocol is an IEEE standard of 802.1ab. Most Cisco devices can perform LLDP.

questions.question: You want to turn off CDP on a switch. Which command would you enter?
questions.explanation: The command to turn off CDP globally on a switch is no cdp run .

questions.question: How often are CDP frames sent out of the device by default?
questions.explanation: CDP frames are sent out all active interfaces every 60 seconds.

questions.question: Which Cisco proprietary protocol collects information from neighboring devices about their identity and capabilities?
questions.explanation: Cisco Discovery Protocol, or CDP, is a Cisco proprietary protocol used for gathering information from neighboring switches and routers.

questions.question: What is the default value of the CDP holddown timer for CDP entries?
questions.explanation: The default holddown timer for CDP entries is three times the advertisement timer of 60 seconds. So entries have a holddowntimer value of 180 seconds.

questions.question: You want to turn off CDP on a single interface. Which command would you enter?
questions.explanation: To turn off or suppress CDP advertisements on a single interface, you would enter the interface and enter the command no cdp enable .

questions.question: Which command gives information that’s identical to the output of the show cdp neighbors detail command?
questions.explanation: The sh cdp entry * command will give output that’s identical to that of the show cdp neighbors detail command.

questions.question: You have several non-Cisco IP phones and you want to allow automatic power adjustments on the Cisco Power over an Ethernet (PoE) switch. Which command will allow you to achieve this?
questions.explanation: The command lldp run entered in global config mode will enable LLDP on all interfaces. When enabled, LLDP-MED, or LLDP for Media, will read capabilities on the phone such as name and power level.

questions.question: Which command will allow you to see LLDP devices connected to a switch?
questions.explanation: The command show lldp neighbor detail will show output identical to the output of show cdp neighbor detail .

questions.question: What is the default LLDP advertisement interval?
questions.explanation: The default LLDP advertisement interval is 30 seconds. When turned on, it will advertise out all active interfaces every 30 seconds.

questions.question: You want to disable LLDP from sending advertisements on a single interface. Which command will you use?
questions.explanation: When you use the command no lldp transmit , it will suppress LLDP messages from exiting the interface it is configured on.

questions.question: What is the default value of the LLDP holddown timer for entries?
questions.explanation: The default value of the LLDP holddown timer for entries is 120 seconds. This holddown timer is set every time the switch hears an advertisement for a device. The holddown is four times the advertisement interval.

questions.question: You have a layer 2 connection to your ISP. You want to make sure that you do not send information on the capabilities of your switch, but you don’t want to affect the use of CDP. Which command will you configure?
questions.explanation: The command no cdp enable will turn off CDP advertisements on the interface that you configure it on.

questions.question: Which command will show the interfaces that CDP is advertising on?
questions.explanation: The command show cdp interface will display all of the interfaces CDP is enabled on along with their advertisement intervals.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of interfaces that can be aggregated with EtherChannel and PAgP?
questions.explanation: EtherChannel can aggregate 2 interfaces to 8 interfaces together on a single switch when using PAgP.

questions.question: Which is a true statement about EtherChannel?
choices: EtherChannel can aggregate multiple lines with varying speed.
When configured, EtherChannel acts as a single layer 2 connection.
EtherChannel works with 802.1Q to block the redundant lines.
EtherChannel can aggregate interfaces across multiple stand-alone switches.
questions.explanation: When EtherChannel bonds interfaces together, they act as a single Ethernet link. Therefore, layer 2 and layer 3 sees it as a single link.

questions.question: You have a switch with 2 Gigabit interface ports and 48 FastEthernet ports and are using PAgP. What is the highest bandwidth you can achieve?
questions.explanation: The highest configurable bandwidth is going to be 2 Gb/s. This is because you cannot mix speeds and duplex.

questions.question: Which negotiation protocol is an IEEE standard?
questions.explanation: The Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) is the IEEE standard 802.3ad.

questions.question: You need to form an EtherChannel between a VMware ESXi host and the switch. Which negotiation protocol will you choose?
questions.explanation: LACP is an IEEE standard that is supported by non-Cisco devices to create aggregation links and negotiate the configuration.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of interfaces that can be aggregated with EtherChannel and LACP?
questions.explanation: EtherChannel can aggregate 2 interfaces to 16 interfaces together on a single switch when using LACP. Only eight ports can be used at any one time; the others are placed in standby mode.

questions.question: Which mode forces the aggregation of links without the use of a control protocol?
questions.explanation: If you configure the EtherChannel to on mode, it forces the aggregation of links together without the use of a control protocol.

questions.question: Which is a correct statement about aggregating ports together?
choices: The term EtherChannel is a Cisco proprietary term for port channeling.
LACP can only be used with other Cisco switches.
PAgP can be used with non-Cisco products.
PAgP can bundle several different speeds and duplexes together.
questions.explanation: The term EtherChannel is a Cisco-centric term. Most vendors will not recognize the term.

questions.question: Which negotiation protocol is a Cisco proprietary standard?
questions.explanation: Port Aggregation Protocol (PAgP) is a Cisco proprietary control negotiation protocol.

questions.question: How often does PAgP send messages to control the status of the links in the bundle?
questions.explanation: PAgP sends control notifications every 30 seconds to the adjacent switch.

questions.question: You want to configure two switches so that LACP is used between the switches. Which mode should you use on both sides to force LACP?
questions.explanation: Using active mode on both sides assures us that the switches will start negotiation with only Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP).

questions.question: What is the effect of configuring a port channel with one side set to passive mode and the other side set to active mode?
choices: The channel group will use LACP.
The channel group will use PAgP.
The channel group will not be formed.
The channel group will use EtherChannel.
questions.explanation: When you use passive on one side and active on the other side of a port channel, the result is that Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) will be used.

questions.question: Which command is used to verify the negotiation protocol for a port channel?
questions.explanation: The command show etherchannel will display all EtherChannels on the switch along with their negotiated protocols.

questions.question: What is the effect of configuring a port channel with one side set to passive mode and the other side set to passive mode?
choices: An unconditional port channel will be formed.
The channel group will use PAgP.
The channel group will use LACP.
The channel group will not be formed.
questions.explanation: Since both interfaces are set to passive mode, neither side will initiate the LACP control notifications. Although the port channel is configured on the switch, it is not communicated between the switches.

questions.question: What is the effect of configuring a port channel with one side set to on mode and the other side set to on mode?
choices: The channel group will use LACP.
The channel group will use PAgP.
An unconditional port-channel will be formed.
The channel group will not be formed.
questions.explanation: When both sides of the port channel are configured with the On mode, an unconditional port channel is created. This means there is no control protocol assisting the port channel.

questions.question: When a port channel is configured, where do you configure the native VLAN?
choices: On the first port in the channel group
In the port channel created for the channel group
On all of the ports in the channel group
questions.explanation: When you configure the channel group command interfaces, it automatically creates a port channel interface. This pseudo interface should be used for all configurations of the collective ports.

questions.question: What is the effect of configuring a port channel with one side set to auto mode and the other side set to desirable mode?
choices: The channel group will use PAgP.
The channel group will not be formed.
An unconditional port channel will be formed.
The channel group will use LACP.
questions.explanation: When one side of the port channel is configured with the auto mode and the other is configured with desirable mode, the EtherChannel is formed with PAgP.

questions.question: Which command will configure one side of an EtherChannel, when the other side is configured with on mode?
choices: SwitchA(config-if)#switchport channel-group 1 mode on SwitchB(config-if)#switchport channel-group 1 mode on
SwitchA(config-if)#switchport channel-group 1 mode desirable SwitchB(config-if)#switchport channel-group 1 mode desirable
SwitchA(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode on SwitchB(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode on
SwitchA(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode desirable SwitchB(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode desirable
questions.explanation: When the on mode is used, it means that no aggregation protocol will be used. On the adjacent switch, you must use the on mode.

questions.question: What is the default load balancing configuration for EtherChannel?
questions.explanation: By default, load balancing is performed on frames by the source MAC address.

questions.question: You want to configure two switches to form a PAgP EtherChannel. Which commands would you enter?
choices: SwitchA(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode desirable SwitchB(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode desirable
SwitchA(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode pagp SwitchB(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode pagp
SwitchA(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode pagp SwitchB(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode pagp
SwitchA(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode desirable SwitchB(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode desirable
questions.explanation: When configuring PAgP, you will use either the auto and desirable mode or the desirable mode on both sides. When you use desirable mode on both sides, desirable mode will unconditionally configure the EtherChannel with PAgP.

questions.question: Which command will change the load-balancing criteria of the EtherChannel for the destination IP?
questions.explanation: When changing the EtherChannel load-balancing criteria, you must change it in global configuration mode via the port-channel load-balance dst-ip command.

questions.question: Which command is used to verify the load-balancing method the switch is using?
questions.explanation: Since the load-balancing method is globally configured, you use the show etherchannel load-balance command to verify the criteria load balancing is performed with.

questions.question: You have a router connected to the switch via an EtherChannel. Which type of load- balancing criteria will you use to make sure you have the most optimal load balancing?
questions.explanation: When you want optimal load balancing, you would configure the source and destination IP address. On some versions of Cisco IOS, you can configure the source and destination IP address as well as the source and destination ports. Although this creates the most optimal load balancing, it creates a high amount of latency since layer 4 information must be calculated.

questions.question: What does the non-silent option along with the mode of auto or desirable do?
choices: Configures the interface to send negotiation notifications
Configures the interface to forward all CDP notifications
Configures the interface not to send negotiation notifications
Configures the interface to send negotiation notifications only if detected
questions.explanation: This option forces an interface, if configured with desirable or auto, to forcibly send notifications. When a port is configured in auto mode, it requires another adjacent switch to send PAgP notifications. This option forces the notifications with the desirable mode.

questions.question: When a port-channel is configured, where do you configure the access VLAN for connection to a server?
choices: All of the ports in the channel group
The first port in the channel group
In the port-channel created for the channel group
questions.explanation: When configuring an access port for use with an EtherChannel, it is recommended to configure the switchport access vlan # command in each interface where the channel-group command has been configured.

questions.question: You have configured the command channel-group 1 mode active on a range of interfaces that will participate in an EtherChannel. Which pseudo interface is created for overall management of the EtherChannel?
questions.explanation: When you configure the channel-group 1 mode active command on the first interface, a pseudo interface is created called port-channel 1. All statistics and configuration should be referenced by this interface.

questions.question: You have several 3750 switches located in the same switch closet. You need to add another switch but are out of Gigabit uplink ports. Which technology could you employ with these switches for optimal bandwidth?
questions.explanation: Switch stacking allows for all of the switches to be tied together so the uplink port can be shared at a nominal bandwidth of 32 Gb/s for the backplane loop.
questions.topic: 2.10 Describe the benefits of switch stacking and chassis aggregation

questions.question: You have several switches configured in a switch stack configuration. You want to make the EtherChannel resilient to failure. Which feature should you use?
questions.explanation: Cross-stack EtherChannel allows you to configure EtherChannels between physical switches to act as one EtherChannel. If one switch or SPF transceiver goes bad, the rest of the switching will be supported by the other physical switches.
questions.topic: 2.10 Describe the benefits of switch stacking and chassis aggregation

questions.question: What is the supported maximum number of 3750 switches that can stacked?
questions.explanation: Cisco will support a maximum of 9 switches in a switch stack configuration.
questions.topic: 2.10 Describe the benefits of switch stacking and chassis aggregation

questions.question: You have three switches with LAN Base and two switches with IP Base features sets. You want to stack the switches together. What needs to be done?
choices: The switch stack will upgrade or downgrade the IOS according to the master switch.
Downgrade the two switches from IP Base to LAN base.
Upgrade the three switches from LAN Base to IP Base.
questions.explanation: When you create a switch stack, the subordinate switches will upgrade or downgrade the IOS software according to the master switch’s IOS. Legally, you must purchase the highest IOS the master switch contains or downgrade the license the master contains.
questions.topic: 2.10 Describe the benefits of switch stacking and chassis aggregation

questions.question: How does traffic flow on the StackWise 3750 platform?
choices: Counter rotation paths at 32 Gb/s each
Counter rotation paths at 16 Gb/s each
questions.explanation: The StackWise 3750 has a backend loop of two counter-rotating rings. Each ring supplies 16 Gb/s in each direction. This allows for up to 32 Gb/s total traffic flow and also allows for redundancy.
questions.topic: 2.10 Describe the benefits of switch stacking and chassis aggregation

questions.question: When you stack Cisco switches together, how do you manage the switch stack?
choices: All switches in a stack need to have contiguous IP addressing.
The entire stack is managed by one IP, and a port number is incremented from 22 for each switch’s logical identity.
The entire stack is managed by the master switch IP.
Each switch has its own logical IP address.
questions.explanation: When you create a switch stack, you assign the IP address to the master switch. This IP address is used for the entire switch stack. If a master fails, a new master is elected and the original master IP is used.

questions.question: You have a switch in a switch stack that has gone bad. You have received a replacement switch and want to swap it out. How can you swap out the bad switch?
choices: You can swap the defective switch while the stack is on and then the stack requires a reload.
You must power the entire stack down to replace the defective switch.
You must add the new switch to the last stack member number in the stack and then remove the defective switch.
You can remove the defective switch while the stack is on and replace it with the replacement switch.
questions.explanation: Switches participating in stacking can be added, deleted, or replaced without powering the stack off. The provisioned switch that is being replaced must match the replacement’s stack member number via the switch {stack-member-number} provision command.

questions.question: Which switch in a stack is responsible for forwarding tables and the central ACL?
questions.explanation: The master switch is responsible for forwarding tables, ACL distribution, QOS, and multicast routing. The master switch is elected by the criteria of configured priority, hardware and software priority, configuration, uptime, and MAC address.

questions.question: You have a switch in a stack that needs to be replaced. You are concerned that the configuration will be lost for the switch. What will happen when it is replaced?
choices: The replacement switch will need to have the configuration TFTP transferred after replacement manually by the network admin.
The replacement switch will need to have its configuration transferred from the existing switch to be replaced.
The replacement switch will need manual configuration since the interfaces will be renumbered.
The replacement switch will automatically download the configuration for the switch member number it’s configured for from the master.
questions.explanation: Configuration is downloaded to the replacement switch automatically when it is replaced. The switch responsible for hosting the configuration is the master switch.

questions.question: You want to upgrade the stack’s IOS. Assuming you have all the same model of switches in the stack, what needs to be done?
choices: Each switch needs to be upgraded independently.
Each switch in the stack needs to be configured with a TFTP location to boot from, and then they all must be reloaded.
The IOS image cannot be changed once a stack is configured.
Only the master switch needs to be upgraded.
questions.explanation: Only the master switch needs to be upgraded. Once the master switch is upgraded, it will download the IOS to all other members of the switch stack.

questions.question: Which switch type in a switch stack downloads it configuration, forwarding table, and ACLs?
questions.explanation: The subordinate switch, often referred to as the slave switch, downloads all of its IOS, configuration, and forwarding tables from the master switch.

questions.question: What is the maximum length of a stacking cable for switch stacks?
questions.explanation: Switch stacking cables come in lengths of 50 centimeters, 1 meter, and 3 meters. The maximum length of the switch stack cable is 3 meters, or about 10 feet.

questions.question: You are connected to a switch stack and want to verify how the stack is cabled. Which command would you use?
questions.explanation: The command used to verify cabling of the switch stack is show switch stack-ports . This command will display a table of how the switches are connected.

questions.question: You want to verify the master switch in the switch stack, which command will display this information?
questions.explanation: The command show switch will display all switches in the stack along with their role. Within this information will be a switch labeled master .

questions.question: You want to make sure that the top switch in the stack always becomes the master. How can you guarantee it always wins the election?
questions.explanation: Priority values can be configured from 1 to 15. The higher the priority, the better the chances of winning an election. If the switch is set to a priority of 15, it will always win the election and become the master.
